tasks.short: Analyze security measures for cyber-defense initiatives

steps.what: Define the security question and verify authorised evidence scope and data quality
Filter known log fields and tabulate security-measure observations
Interpret predictive or reactive findings and challenge alternative security explanations
Write and check the internal security-analysis findings and limitations

tasks.design: Configure saved read-only queries and tables in the {DATA_PLATFORM} over verified copies from the forensic-analysis category {OTHER}. Keep scope, evidence-quality checks, interpretation and the actual internal report human; native query reuse removes repeated filtering and tallying, not predictive judgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Analysts repeatedly prepare comparable log summaries while source gaps can change the conclusion.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned native queries can reuse verified field mappings and filters.
tasks.still_hard: Attribution, confounding factors and whether observed control effectiveness generalises.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge the evidence and avoid treating correlations as incident causes.
tasks.altitude: More attention to security interpretations and less repeated tabulation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: saved queries can deterministically filter known log fields and generate tables, while security interpretation remains analyst judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is analysis and its existing internal findings report, not incident containment or regulator notification. Shares are provisional.

Source-system custodians supply authorised copies with source identifier, event timestamp/timezone, event type and relevant control outcomes; the analyst verifies provenance, scope and field meaning in s1. Unknown formats and missing fields are manually mapped or excluded with limitations in retained s1/s3; no free extraction or new logging is assumed.

Test native saved queries first. s2 represents today's repeated human query setup, filtering and tallying, not existing automatic runtime. Failed or incomparable queries return to manual analysis within retained s3. Nothing writes to original evidence.

Original report writing and ordinary saving remain fully retained and ungated in s4. Actual external report sends or control changes require separate final-version approval and action steps; none is hidden in analysis. Existing source collection labour is not claimed saved.
research_questions: Can native queries reproduce checked tables across known log sources without new capture or changed evidence?

already_counted.description: Source checks, mapping exceptions, manual query repair and interpretation remain.

incremental.description: Analyst validates saved queries after log schema or control changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 25 repeated filtering/tally hours removed less 1.5 upkeep gives 23.5 net. Cautious case: legacy log schemas require manual mapping and only 4 hours of known-field tabulation are removed, giving 2.5 net; interpretation and report writing stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write and execute forensic automation scripts

steps.what: Specify the parsing task, authorised evidence copies and expected output contract
Write the data-parsing or task-automation script

loop.purpose: Draft parsing code against an explicit evidence-copy input and output contract
loop.input: checked specification, schema and analyst-created non-sensitive fixtures
loop.check: Analyst checks code meaning and runs fixtures for record completeness, timestamps/timezones, encodings, malformed rows, hashes and absence of writes to evidence
loop.stop: Unclear schema, prohibited access or two failed candidates means manual coding in retained time
loop.why_not_simpler: Use native forensic export/parser configuration first; residual source-specific parsing logic needs code that is checked against explicit fixtures

steps.what: Test the script on fixtures and representative copies and repair failures
outputs: tested forensic script and validation results

steps.what: Review the final script hash, evidence-copy inputs and exact output destination
inputs: tested forensic script and validation results
outputs: authorised script version and execution scope

steps.what: Execute the approved script on the exact authorised evidence copies
inputs: authorised script version and execution scope
outputs: derived forensic output and execution record

tasks.design: Try native forensic parsers and export configuration first, then use a bounded code-drafting loop for the remaining source-specific parser in the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Keep specification, fixture creation, testing, repair and final execution-scope review; run only the approved script version on authorised copies with a separate derived-output destination.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source-specific parsing code is repetitive but can silently lose or alter forensic meaning.
tasks.enabler_now: Code drafting can shorten initial implementation after the analyst defines and tests the contract.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual encodings, malformed records, timezone meaning and proving completeness.
tasks.human_edge: Define evidentially correct outputs and recognise misleading parser success.
tasks.altitude: Less initial coding, with the same evidential validation and execution authority.

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot supports code completion and coding assistance with expected oversight; this supports draft-code capability, not forensic correctness or the proposed saving.

assumptions: Boundary is writing and running a script for already authorised forensic processing, not new access, live containment or modifying originals. Shares are provisional.

The analyst defines file types, encoding, source hashes, expected fields, record counts, timestamp semantics, error policy and output schema and creates fixtures in s1. No free structured specification, labelled test data or unpriced evidence acquisition is assumed.

Native parsers first. Only initial code entry and routine implementation, 50% of s2, are removed; analyst review and manual rewrite remain in s2, with independent fixture/integration testing and repairs fully retained in s3. Existing script runtime is excluded from labour.

s4 checks the completed tested script hash, exact input-copy hashes, permissions and derived-output path before execution s5; edits or scope changes void approval. This gate authorises an actual run, not an ordinary author save; draft saves are fully retained and ungated.

If a second examiner is required, add that actual actor and labour before execution; this branch assumes the analyst already holds this scoped execution authority. Findings interpretation remains a separate analysis task.
unknowns: Actual initial coding versus testing effort
research_questions: Can assisted code pass complete-record, malformed-input and timezone fixtures without additional review or repair?

already_counted.description: Draft review, manual coding repair, fixture tests and final run-scope checks remain.

incremental.description: Analyst revalidates assisted-code behaviour and parser dependencies after updates.

approvals.approved_version: s4 tested final script hash, exact input-copy hashes, permissions and derived-output destination; any code or scope edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 35*0.50=17.5 initial coding hours removed less 2 upkeep gives 15.5 net. Cautious case: an undocumented binary format requires manual parser design and most code is rewritten, leaving only 3 hours of routine file-handling code removed and 1 net; all testing and final scope review remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Recommend cyber-defense software or hardware for incident response

steps.what: Establish incident-response gaps, evidence constraints and required capabilities
Examine candidate software or hardware documentation and trial evidence
Compare capability fit, operational burden and evidential limitations
Write the cyber-defense recommendation and source-linked comparison
Check the final recommendation, evidence and internal decision-maker destination
outputs: final checked defense recommendation and destination

steps.what: Send the checked recommendation to the internal security decision maker
inputs: final checked defense recommendation and destination

tasks.design: Reuse the existing {DOCS} incident-response recommendation headings and capability-comparison columns. The analyst reviews evidence from the forensic-analysis category {OTHER}, judges candidate fit and writes the recommendation; its internal send follows checking the completed version and recipient.
tasks.previous_blocker: Defense recommendations depend on incident-specific gaps and reliable candidate evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document structure can remove repeated report formatting.
tasks.still_hard: Compatibility, unproven vendor claims and operational cost of a proposed defense.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a capability demonstration from a credible incident-response fit.
tasks.altitude: Less report layout; unchanged recommendation and procurement boundaries.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed recommendation headings and comparison-column layouts can be reused while product evidence and suitability judgement remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is an actual recommendation read by the security decision maker, not purchasing, installation or live defense changes. Shares are provisional.

The analyst checks actual incident findings and defense inventory in s1; candidate suppliers provide original documentation and separately authorised trials provide results, all reviewed in s2. No structured product feed, new trial execution or free comparison extraction is assumed. New trials require their own scope, approval and labour.
Test native {DOCS} template first. Only headings and comparison-column layout, 6% of s4, are removed; all capability extraction, evaluation, source checking and ordinary ungated saving remain.
s5 checks the final completed recommendation and exact internal decision maker before s6; edits void approval. No supplier order or system deployment is authorised by the recommendation.
research_questions: Does native layout reuse remove any real formatting beyond the existing recommendation form?

already_counted.description: Candidate evidence review, suitability judgement, substantive writing and final checks remain.

incremental.description: Analyst updates comparison layout when response requirements change.

approvals.approved_version: s5 final checked cyber-defense recommendation, attachments and exact internal security decision-maker destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 20*0.06=1.2 layout hours removed less 0.4 upkeep gives 0.8 net. Cautious case: novel hardware needs a bespoke comparison matrix, leaving 0.5 hours of standard headings removed and 0.1 net; evidence and judgement remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Native query reuse and assisted parser drafting reduce repetitive work; evidential scope, validation, interpretation and recommendations remain with the analyst.
role.ambitious_version: No autonomous evidence alteration, incident containment or commercial deployment is proposed.
